title: Add v2 tool-loop observability and monitor cancellation
objective: Extend the additive llm/request/v2 runtime boundary with reusable DebugSink tool lifecycle events and monitor-triggered cooperative cancellation while preserving v1 contracts and existing bounded tool-loop behavior.

branch.name: wi-0005-v2-observability-cancellation
branch.rationale: The work item is processed as a serial set of scoped commits on the current repository branch; the branch name records the intended v2 capability boundary without requiring a topic branch.

request.text: Prepare a new .docs/work-items/* in the llm repository for additive llm/request/v2 observability and monitor-triggered cancellation. Reuse DebugSink for tool lifecycle events and cancellation signaling, preserve v1, do not extend scope into LangGraph embedding, persistence, or unrelated request-schema edits. Review for correctness/consistency and commit the documentation.

scope.name: v2-debug-tool-events
scope.description: Reuse DebugSink to emit bounded llm.tool.batch.start, llm.tool.call, llm.tool.result, and llm.tool.batch.end events for automatic v2 tool execution without changing existing JSONL stderr delivery.
scope.reason: Monitors need visibility into tool-heavy workloads, including parallel call correlation and sanitized results, while the existing debug boundary is already integrated with the package and CLI.

scope.name: v2-monitor-cancellation
scope.description: Use the existing runtime AbortSignal option as a cooperative cancellation signal, propagate it to provider fetches and injected tools, stop future loop work, preserve completed results, and return a bounded v2 cancelled response with cancellation events.
scope.reason: A monitor that can observe a run must be able to halt expensive or unsafe continued processing without adding callbacks to the serializable request document.

nonGoals.name: v1-contract-mutation
nonGoals.description: Do not change llm/request/v1, llm/response/v1, or their behavior.
nonGoals.reason: The v1 contracts are closed compatibility boundaries and the requested capability is additive to v2.

nonGoals.name: new-observer-api
nonGoals.description: Do not add a second response observer, callback field, event-stream abstraction, or callback value to llm/request/v2; reuse DebugSink through runtime completion options.
nonGoals.reason: The existing DebugSink already provides sanitized, JSONL-compatible event delivery and the request contract must remain serializable.

nonGoals.name: langgraph-runtime
nonGoals.description: Do not add LangGraph, a native graph runtime, persistence, checkpointing, resume, or graph-level scheduling to the llm package.
nonGoals.reason: Provider transport and bounded convenience orchestration remain separate from the authoritative graph runtime in downstream consumers.

nonGoals.name: unrelated-worktree-changes
nonGoals.description: Do not stage or modify the pre-existing request-schema edits outside this work item.
nonGoals.reason: Those changes predate WI-0005 and are unrelated to v2 observability and cancellation.

nonGoals.name: operational-expansion
nonGoals.description: Do not claim authenticated provider behavior, real external tool side effects, rollback, forced termination of arbitrary code, production deployment, or downstream integration.
nonGoals.reason: The work item is limited to local provider-free contracts, cooperative runtime cancellation, deterministic tests, and package documentation.

items.name: tool-lifecycle-debug-events
items.description: Automatic v2 tool execution emits sanitized lifecycle events for sequential batches, individual calls, individual results, and batch completion through the existing DebugSink.
items.reason: Monitors need to observe tool-heavy workloads and correlate parallel calls without introducing a second event transport.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Deterministic tests verify llm.tool.batch.start, llm.tool.call, llm.tool.result, and llm.tool.batch.end events, including round, batchIndex, callId, sanitized result status, and parallel result correlation.

items.name: cooperative-cancellation-control
items.description: A runtime AbortSignal can cancel a v2 completion before or during provider and tool work, and cancellation is observed without starting later retries, tool batches, or model requests.
items.reason: A monitor needs a control path that can halt continued processing while preserving the existing serializable request contract.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Deterministic tests cover an already-aborted signal, cancellation during provider fetch, cancellation during a tool call, cancellation during a parallel batch, and no work beginning after cancellation is observed.

items.name: cancellation-propagation-and-response
items.description: Provider requests and ToolInvocationContext receive the cancellation signal, completed bounded results remain available, and v2 returns a terminal cancelled response with sanitized cancellation diagnostics.
items.reason: Cancellation must be observable and actionable without misclassifying it as an ordinary provider or tool failure.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The response/v2 contract and implementation represent cancelled with a bounded CANCELLED diagnostic, tests verify provider/tool signal identity and preserved completed results, and cancellation is not retried.

items.name: v2-compatibility-and-scope
items.description: The implementation remains additive to v2, preserves v1 behavior, retains DebugSink failure isolation and redaction, and does not add LangGraph or absorb unrelated worktree changes.
items.reason: The requested capability is safe to add before v2 downstream consumers exist, but its compatibility and repository boundaries must remain explicit.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Typecheck, deterministic tests, build, schema-example validation, static scope inspection, and diff checks pass; v1 regression coverage remains green; no LangGraph dependency or pre-existing request-schema edit is staged.
